options.B: It disrupts the mucosal barrier, increasing susceptibility to HIV and other STIs
options.C: It prevents the transmission of viral pathogens
options.D: It has no relationship with STI acquisition

explanation: Inflammation and disruption of the vaginal mucosal barrier significantly increase a woman's vulnerability to acquiring HIV and other STIs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h9)

question: Through which valve does blood pass when moving from the right atrium to the right ventricle?

options.A: Mitral valve
options.B: Aortic valve
options.C: Tricuspid valve
options.D: Pulmonary valve

explanation: The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium from the right ventricle, ensuring one-way blood flow. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is identified as one of the leading causes of faecal incontinence among women in Nigerian clinical practice?

options.A: Appendectomy
options.B: Obstetric trauma from prolonged or obstructed labour
options.C: Peptic ulcer disease
options.D: Primary hypertension

explanation: Obstetric trauma, including perineal tears from prolonged or obstructed labour, is a leading cause of faecal incontinence in women. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: What are striae gravidarum commonly known as?

options.A: Spider veins
options.B: Stretch marks
options.C: Birthmarks
options.D: Hives

explanation: Striae gravidarum are commonly referred to as stretch marks, caused by skin stretching and alterations in collagen and elastic tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: What is the standard recommended timeline for a follow-up clinic visit when a client initiates a new oral contraceptive method?

options.A: After exactly one week
options.B: After three months to assess tolerance and compliance
options.C: Only after two years of continuous use
options.D: At the start of the next calendar year

explanation: A three-month follow-up allows nurses to evaluate how well the client is tolerating the medication, manage initial side effects, and ensure correct usage. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h8)

question: What role does transportation infrastructure play in the food supply chain?

options.A: It acts as the circulatory system that moves food from surplus zones to deficit areas.
options.B: It determines the chemical composition of the soil.
options.C: It controls the amount of rainfall an agricultural region receives.
options.D: It replaces the need for irrigation systems.

explanation: Transport networks connect producers to consumers, allowing food to be moved efficiently before it spoils. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h7)

question: How can taking analgesics for right lower quadrant abdominal pain be dangerous in the context of appendicitis?

options.A: It cures the appendicitis instantly without surgery
options.B: It masks symptoms, delaying surgical intervention until rupture and peritonitis occur
options.C: It lowers the patient's blood pressure permanently
options.D: It turns the appendix into a healthy organ

explanation: Analgesics mask critical pain signals of appendicitis, delaying diagnosis and leading to dangerous complications like rupture and peritonitis. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)
